Dockerfile instructions that restore packages from precompiled binaries

Source: R/sysreqs-helpers.R
dot-binary_restore_instructions.Rd

Posit Package Manager serves precompiled Linux binaries at .../cran/__linux__/<codename>/<snapshot>. Restoring from there skips compilation, which is where almost all of a source restore's time goes. The binaries are still linked against system libraries, so the apt-get block that .fetch_sysreqs() and install_syslibs build is needed just as much as for a source restore. The -dev packages in it also pull in the matching runtime libraries, for instance libwebpmux3 through libwebp-dev.

Usage

.binary_restore_instructions(image_os_version, snapshot = "latest")

Arguments

image_os_version

Character. The Ubuntu release backing the image's FROM line, from .resolve_os_version().

snapshot

Character. "latest" or a "YYYY-MM-DD" snapshot date.

Value

A character vector of two RUN instructions, or NULL when there is no codename for image_os_version, in which case the caller keeps the source restore.

Details

The codename must name the Ubuntu release the image is actually built on, not the release a system-requirements lookup was asked about, since a binary built for one release is not guaranteed to load on another.
